title: New York City Department of Homeless Services – Oversight of Contract Expenditures of Samaritan Daytop Village, Inc. (Follow-Up)
plain_title: Checkup on oversight of a homeless shelter contractor's spending
agency: New York City Department of Social Services
what_they_audited: How far the New York City Department of Homeless Services has gone in carrying out the six recommendations from a 2024 state audit of its contract with Samaritan Daytop Village, Inc.
background: The Department of Homeless Services contracted with the nonprofit Samaritan Daytop Village to run the 160-bed Myrtle Avenue Men's Shelter for men with mental illness, a contract that grew to about $44 million through June 2022. The initial audit found the department was not effectively monitoring the contract and identified $566,556 in reported costs that did not comply with fiscal requirements.

findings.plain: The department has made some progress since the initial audit but more work remains. Of the six original recommendations, five were partially implemented and one was not implemented.
findings.quote: Of the initial report’s six audit recommendations, five were partially implemented and one was not implemented.

numbers.label: Noncompliant costs found by the initial audit
Approximate aggregate cost of the shelter contract

recommendations: Department of Homeless Services officials are asked, though not required, to report within 30 days on any actions planned to address the unresolved issues.
